note: Locale-NEUTRAL. The jar shows pictures and the ritual counts them, so no per-locale word bank exists — the only spoken content is bare numerals. Season keys come from SEASONAL_KEYS in frontend/lib/seasonal-hub.ts; only the UNIVERSAL five are used (christmas/easter/winter/spring/summer), because 4th_of_july and thanksgivinng are en-only there and these objects are not culture-bound. Autumn has no theme key in the library at all, so acorns/pinecones/leaves ship season-null rather than mis-tagged.
packNote: v2 adds `pack` per set, and it is load-bearing rather than decorative. The jar now draws exactly N real objects, so the pile height IS the quantity — which means the objects must be sized by the INK inside the sprite, not by the sprite canvas. Every canvas is square; measured coverage of the ink inside it spans 3.29x (snowflakes 0.205 -> seashells 0.674), so one global object size would make a jar of seashells read three times fuller than a jar of snowflakes at the SAME N. That is the exact dishonesty this rebuild removes, reintroduced one layer down. r70 = radius (fraction of canvas) of the disc about the alpha centroid holding 70% of the alpha mass — the PACKING radius, which deliberately discounts thin appendages (a cherry stem, a lollipop stick) because those should be allowed to overlap a neighbour. cy = alpha centroid Y as a fraction of the canvas; objects draw at -S*cy so the visual mass lands on the packed point (without it a lollipop's candy floats a sixth of a canvas high). cx measured 0.484-0.523 across all sets — tight enough that the draw call needs no cx term. rotMax = rotation half-range in degrees: the sprites carry BAKED directional light, so free rotation lights the pile from every direction at once and reads as stickers; radially symmetric sets tolerate 40. GENERATED BY scripts/measure-jar-sprites.js — do not hand-edit; verify-estimation-jar.js re-derives these from the sprites and fails on disagreement.
capacityNote: The JAR NEVER CHANGES SIZE between capacities — the OBJECTS do. A 30-jar has big objects, a 200-jar has small ones. Three physically different glasses would destroy cross-session comparison: a child cannot tell whether today's jar holds more than yesterday's if the glass itself changed. Capacity is the teacher's choice and it drives the object size, the pile height and the number line's range — never the subscription tier, which is what the v1 tool did.
